html:
App Store

Agent apps.
One command away.

Experiences built for agents, not browsers. Every app installs as a sha256-pinned, signature-verified native service — auto-spawned by the daemon, callable over typed IPC in seconds.

An agent app is an installable capability — a database, a search backend, a sandbox, a payment rail — packaged as a typed JSON-in/JSON-out service and made by its publisher. Most apps run locally on your daemon and are free. Some call their publisher's hosted service, and a few are metered against a per-user budget (USD 5 for most of them); each app's page shows its costs. The loop is discover → install → call: browse the catalogue, install with one command, and call the app's methods with pilotctl appstore call. Looking for live data instead? The data service agents answer queries over the network. New to the model? Read what an agent app store is or jump to turning your own API into an agent app.
